name: AI literacy
description: Using AI chatbots well for study: asking precise questions and checking what they say.

name: Asking and checking
description: Phrasing a question a chatbot can answer well and checking its claims against independent sources.

name: Ask: a precise question
description: Phrasing a precise, answerable question: the idea, the setting (place and time), and asking for sources and reasoning.
intuition: A vague question gets a vague answer; a precise one gets something you can use and check.

name: Verify: check a claim
description: Checking a chatbot's claim against an independent source: open it, note who published it and when, compare, and say whether it matched.
intuition: Fact-checkers leave the page to see what other sources say before trusting it.

name: How AI chatbots work
description: Why chatbots fail the way they do: invented sources, false confidence, a training cut-off and agreeing with the user.

name: Why chatbots invent sources
description: Chatbots generate likely-looking text, so a citation or link can look real and not exist.
intuition: A chatbot predicts likely words, and a citation is just more likely-looking words.

name: Why confidence isn't evidence
description: A chatbot's tone says nothing about whether its answer is right.
intuition: A chatbot uses the same sure tone whether it is right or wrong.

name: Why chatbots miss recent events
description: Without a web search, a chatbot only knows what was in its training text, up to a date.
intuition: A chatbot learned from text up to a date, and newer events weren't in it.

name: Why chatbots agree with you
description: Chatbots can change a right answer to agree with a user who pushes back.
intuition: Chatbots are trained to please, so pushing back can make them give in.
